page.layout: One column of running text, with Greek and Latin quotations set in italic and a Greek verse stanza. No marginal notes. Catchword "Ad" at the lower right.

main_text.p: fi è manu flaminis commentaculum virga excidi-fet: fed quoties aliquid excidiffet, puta fpondeum vt hoc loco Theophrasti: aut victima, vel τὰ σωλά-χνα, vt Craffo accidit. aut de capite sacrificantis vitta, quod de Syrhace canit Silius Italicus. Simile eft quod notat Cicero De aruspicum responsis, lu-dos esse non rite factos, fi puer patrimus & matri-mus tensam aut lorum omitteret. Meminerat ite-rum Festus huius superstitionis in voce filere, quan-tum ex iis quae superfunt licet coniicere.

ἀπελάσας ὁ βλάπτων ὑπὲρ τῆς τῷ.) Nihil hoc foedius, nihil spurcius: verùm praeterea notandum est, non δυσχέρειαν tantùm hic esse: sed etiam, vt sunt concatenata vitia, faltum, & conuiuarum contemtum. Olim enim in conuiuiis aut aliis congressionibus, procul spuere signum habebatur eminentiae. Plautus dixit magnificè conscreare: Quintilianus, clare exscreare. Sotades apud Stobaeum:

p.i: Εἰ δ' βασιλεὺς πέφυκας, ὡς ὄντες ἀνέχειν' Ἂν μακρὰ πύλης, φλεγμαίνει κραλῆ ἀξιοσῳ' Ἀνιδίματῆς, ταῦτα προ τε προβατικὸν ἔχεν.

main_text.p: Praeclarè verò Clemens Alexandrinus, de hoc ipso loquens 1 1. Paedagogi, ἐν ἐρωχίας δ' ἀξίας συμβολον, τὸ προδεῖναι τὶς ἡχοῖς ἐθέλειν, μὴ ἀχί ἀφαιρεῖν. Sic & plurimum tuffire potentiorum erat tantum. Petronius, Secundum hanc formulam imperamus Eu-molpo vt plurimum tussiat, vt fit solutioris stomachi, ci-bosque omnes palam damnet, loquatur aurum & argen-tum, fundi fque mendaces. Erant item argumenta po-tentiae cervices inflectere, & altum loqui, vt ex Plu-tarchi Pyrrho & Demosthene intelligitur.

page.notes: Greek passages are uncertain in several letters (e.g. the opening Greek word of the second paragraph, the verse stanza and the Clemens quotation); the Greek is transcribed as read, but without certainty and should be checked against the scan. The Greek parenthesis at the opening of the second paragraph is marked as a whole for the same reason. The Greek of the Sotades stanza has its first line partly illegible. "conscreare" is read from the print; the scan's letters are close to "conscreare" and may be a printing variant. The catchword "Ad" is at the foot right.
